videos.script: Every lesson so far has used wg.Go and promised the details. Here they are. {{wait}} A WaitGroup is a counter of goroutines still running. Add raises it, Done lowers it, Wait blocks until it reaches zero. You write the three calls by hand, then watch the common mistake. Add inside the goroutine. Five goroutines start, and Wait returns before any of them finish. go vet catches it, and wg.Go makes it impossible. {{once}} Next, doing something exactly once. Eight goroutines ask for a configuration, and it loads once. Then OnceValues, which caches an error as faithfully as a result. The file appears, and the error stays. {{map}} Last, maps. Four goroutines write to an ordinary map, and the runtime stops the program. sync.Map is safe, and its own documentation says most code should not use it. {{close}} Lesson 10 starts the context package.
